name: coupled-fate-oscillator
title: Coupled cell: an ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS fate network form a metabolism↔fate oscillator

behavior_tests.name: fate-oscillates
behavior_tests.description: Over the run the fate 'divide' activity (emitted as probe_a) crosses the 0.5 cutoff at least twice — the metabolism↔fate loop oscillates rather than latching.

limitations: The quantitative period/amplitude are not pinned to an acceptance band yet (only the presence of oscillation is a committed test).
MaBoSS mean-field istate adds ~5% noise and a one-step lag that sets the period.
claim: Two sub-cellular simulators of different formalisms — an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS Boolean fate network — can be coupled inside one cell in both directions (the ODE's metabolite C pins the fate 'high_C' input, mode A; the fate 'divide' output resets the metabolism, mode C) to produce a metabolism↔fate feedback oscillator that neither formalism exhibits alone.
experiment: Run coupled_fate_oscillator (a small vertex tissue of CoupledCells) for 40 steps. Record one cell's metabolite C and fate 'divide' each step.
outcomes: The time series (viz/coupled-fate-oscillator.html) shows a stable oscillation: C builds over ~2 steps, crosses the threshold, pins high_C, the fate 'divide' fires, the division resets the metabolism, and the cycle repeats (period ~3 steps). Computed live from real tellurium + MaBoSS engines.

axis.label: Over the run the fate 'divide' activity (emitted as probe_a) crosses the 0.5 cutoff at least twice — the metabolism↔fate loop oscillates rather than latching.

question: Can an SBML-ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS Boolean fate network be coupled inside one cell, in both directions, to produce a metabolism<->fate feedback oscillator that neither formalism shows alone?

study_card.goal: Show that two sub-cellular simulators of different formalisms couple into a metabolism<->fate feedback oscillator inside one cell.
study_card.mechanism: Two sub-cellular formalisms in one cell: an ODE metabolism and a MaBoSS fate network, coupled both ways (mode A: metabolite C pins the fate 'high_C' input; mode C: the fate 'divide' output resets the metabolism). The result is a stable period-3 metabolism<->fate oscillator.
study_card.why_before_next: The two-way coupling (modes A+C) is the minimal CoupledCell motif the rest of the atlas builds on; proving it oscillates validates the coupling contract itself.
study_card.expected_result: The fate 'divide' node oscillates (>=2 threshold crossings), so the ODE<->MaBoSS coupling produces a genuine metabolism<->fate feedback cycle.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is a mean-field MaBoSS istate (with its one-step lag) an acceptable stand-in for a stochastic fate network when the fate output gates a fast metabolic reset?
